name: Grown Rogue Gardens LLC N Foothill

nadir.desc: The property consists of a large cultivated agricultural field with dense parallel rows of green plants|Multiple long greenhouse or tunnel structures are located near the field|A man-made pond is present on the site|Dirt access roads and open dry ground surround the cultivated areas|The property is located in a rural agricultural setting adjacent to a main road.

alpha.desc: The front of the facility shows open dry terrain and a dirt access road leading toward the cultivated field|Long greenhouse structures and the pond are visible|The large field of parallel plant rows extends across the main portion of the property.

bravo.desc: The left side of the facility shows the edge of the cultivated field with parallel plant rows|Greenhouse structures and open dry ground are present|Dirt access paths and sparse vegetation continue along this side.

charlie.desc: The rear of the facility shows the full extent of the cultivated field with dense parallel rows of plants|Greenhouse structures, open dry terrain, and dirt roads are visible|The pond and additional open ground are present toward one edge of the property.

delta.desc: The right side of the facility shows the cultivated field edge, greenhouse structures, and the pond|Open dry ground and dirt access roads continue along this side|Sparse vegetation and trees are present near the water feature and field edges.

considerations: Vehicle access is provided by dirt roads that connect from the main paved road to the cultivated field and greenhouse structures. Open dry ground surrounding the field provides space for emergency vehicle staging. The large cultivated area and greenhouse structures occupy the central portion of the property. A pond is present on the site and may serve as a water source. The rural agricultural layout allows relatively open movement around the perimeter, though the dense plant rows and greenhouse structures may limit access within the cultivated zone.
clarifications: Where are the primary vehicle entrances to the property, and are any of them gated or restricted? Is vehicle access available on all sides of the cultivated area? What is the primary crop or use of the greenhouse structures and field rows?
